clue.text: Her kissing takes a lot of beating

definitions.text: Her kissing takes a lot of beating

parts.words: Her kissing takes a lot of beating
parts.note: an old naval idiom: a sailor bent over a cannon to be flogged was said to kiss the gun's 'daughter', so her kiss meant a thrashing

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a woman whose kisses are unbeatable; in fact 'takes a lot of beating' is literal, since kissing her meant being flogged.
explanation.definitionFit: Old naval slang for the cannon a sailor was tied over for a flogging, so kissing her was punishment.

clue.text: Like coteries, perhaps?

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of the following word may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A question asking what quality small exclusive circles share.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns COTERIES into the answer, while the whole clue also defines it: knowledge kept within a coterie is exactly what the word describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood only by a small inner circle, which is what a coterie is.

clue.text: Grave said to contain terrorist leader

indicators.note: to contain means the word said holds another letter inside it
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A solemn report that someone was holding the head of a terror cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to contain' puts T, the first letter of 'terrorist', inside SAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave and staid are synonyms, both meaning serious and sober in manner.

clue.text: Meat in a bun for a picnic

indicators.note: in means the meat goes inside the bun

parts.note: a bun is a small cake
lamb is a kind of meat

explanation.surface: A suggestion of a meat-filled roll to take on a picnic.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's burger is a decoy: the bun is the outer piece, the meat its filling.
explanation.definitionFit: A clambake is an American seaside picnic where clams and other food are cooked outdoors.

clue.text: User did wrong indeed

indicators.note: in means the jumbled letters go inside the word for a deed
wrong signals that the letters of did are put in a mistaken order

explanation.surface: Someone accusing a drug user of misbehaving, 'indeed'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indeed' must be split as 'in deed', the container signal followed by the outer word; 'wrong' scrambles the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A user in the drug sense is someone dependent on a substance, an addict.

clue.text: A harvest with poor soil in Greece

indicators.note: poor signals the letters of soil are in a bad, jumbled state

explanation.surface: A Greek farmer's complaint of a meagre harvest from bad ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is merely 'in Greece': the famous citadel stands above Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: The Acropolis is the ancient citadel found in Athens, so it is something in Greece.

clue.text: Stir up in low state

indicators.note: in means the turned word goes inside the cattle sound

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: stir is slang for prison, as is can

explanation.surface: An order to cause trouble in a depressed nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir' looks like a verb but is a noun, British slang for prison; 'up' turns its synonym in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Monaco is a tiny sovereign principality on the Riviera, a state in its own right.

clue.text: Inscrutable nature of Humpty Dumpty's vocabulary

definitions.meaning: the quality of being impossible to see into or understand
in Through the Looking-Glass Humpty Dumpty uses this very word and explains what he makes it mean

explanation.walkthrough: Lewis Carroll's Humpty Dumpty says this word to Alice, insisting words mean what he chooses them to mean.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that cannot be penetrated or fathomed has this quality, an inscrutable character.

clue.text: Outstanding in flight

definitions.meaning: outstanding as in a bill still owed, not yet paid
a bird in flight has not settled anywhere

explanation.definitionFit: An unpaid debt is not settled, and a flying bird has not settled to rest.

clue.text: Englishman sees nothing in church order

indicators.note: in means the zero goes inside the church and order letters

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: An Englishman finds no place in the church's hierarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: The OM is Britain's Order of Merit, an honour. The Englishman is Australian slang, a cousin of pommy.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian slang for an Englishman, a jokey variant of pom.

clue.text: Old Latin element of north entrance

parts.note: an atrium is an entrance hall

explanation.surface: A classical building component at the northern doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodium's Latin name, which gives it the chemical symbol Na.

clue.text: One that much behind gets set apart

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
so, as in 'so big', means to that extent

explanation.surface: Someone running very late finds themselves left out.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate something is to separate it from others, setting it apart.

clue.text: Poison without copper is not much done

indicators.note: without means the copper symbol is taken out

parts.note: curare is a South American arrow poison
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A remark that poison lacking a metal achieves very little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes CU from CURARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare meat is cooked only briefly, so it is not much done.

clue.text: Swiss banker consumes carved roast, being a man of taste

indicators.note: consumes means the banker swallows the rearranged roast

parts.note: the gnomes of Zurich is a nickname for Swiss bankers

indicators.note: carved signals the roast is cut up and its letters reordered

explanation.surface: A Swiss financier tucks into a carved joint, showing refined taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gnomes of Zurich' was a 1960s British jibe at Swiss bankers; 'carved' scrambles the joint and 'consumes' wraps the banker round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gastronome is a connoisseur of good food, a person of refined palate.

clue.text: Scot in POW camp rising got sent a letter

indicators.note: in means the name goes inside the turned camp word
rising in a down clue means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp
Ian is a typically Scottish name

explanation.surface: A Scottish prisoner of war receives a letter from home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns the camp upward in this down clue, and 'in' sets the Scottish name inside it just before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul's Epistle to the Galatians was a letter addressed to that people, so they received one.

clue.text: Rest at end of year — or of life

definitions.text: Rest at end of year — or of life

indicators.note: at means the rest is placed beside the month that follows it

parts.note: Dec, December, is the year's last month

explanation.surface: Taking a break as the year closes, or as one's life does.
explanation.walkthrough: DEC comes first and EASE is 'at' it; the whole clue then reads as the definition, a final rest at the end of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Decease is a formal word for death, the end of a life.

clue.text: Indicator prepared for one trip

indicators.note: prepared signals that the letters are made ready in a new order

explanation.surface: A signpost set up for a single journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges ONE TRIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointer is something that indicates, like a needle on a dial.

clue.text: Parson started and attained what he did

indicators.note: started means the opening letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A parson began and reached his goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'started' gives the P of 'Parson'. The definition refers back to the parson: what a parson does from the pulpit.
explanation.definitionFit: A parson preaches sermons, so this past tense describes his activity.

clue.text: Opera managed to turn toad into princess

definitions.text: Opera managed to turn toad into princess

indicators.note: managed means handled or arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale opera that transforms a toad into a princess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'managed' rearranges TURN TOAD. The whole clue describes the opera, whose title role is a princess, so this is an all-in-one.
explanation.definitionFit: Puccini's last opera, named after its icy Chinese princess heroine.

clue.text: Mutated virus later found to be beyond our scope

indicators.note: mutated means changed in form, so the letters change order

explanation.surface: A virus that changed later proves too much for scientists to handle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mutated' rearranges VIRUS LATER.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin legal phrase for acting beyond one's authority or powers.

clue.text: Smoke volume cut out by force in the island

indicators.note: cut out by means one piece is removed and another put in its place

parts.note: cc, cubic centimetres, is a measure of volume
g is the symbol for gravitational force

explanation.surface: Tobacco smuggled into an island is seized by police force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut out by' removes CC from TOBACCO and puts G in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobago is a Caribbean island, partner of Trinidad in one nation.

clue.text: Bird's habitat

parts.note: bird is slang for a prison sentence, so its habitat is where a convict lives: in jail

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' looks ornithological, but in British slang doing bird means serving prison time.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for being in prison, which is where someone doing bird lives.

clue.text: There's something fishy about removing lines from bar code

indicators.note: about means the remaining letters are turned round
removing means those letters are taken out

parts.note: the whole word barcode is taken and the poem removed; the reversed run in those letters is a coincidence of the deletion, not a hiding
an ode is a poem, lines of verse

explanation.surface: Suspicion that a barcode has had its stripes taken out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing' and 'about' work in turn. The barcode's printed lines are a decoy: the lines are a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A crab is a sea creature, loosely something from the fishmonger.

clue.text: 25 balloon initially when not blown up

indicators.note: initially means the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A balloon that went limp because it was never inflated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives B. The definition is the answer at 25: David Low's pompous cartoon officer bore this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Low's cartoon officer, a byword for blustering reactionary views, carried this surname.

clue.text: Heartless king with wives, excepting last Catherine of varied stock

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letters of the name are removed

parts.note: Henry is a king, apt beside the wives

indicators.note: excepting means one letter is left out
last means the final letter of Catherine is the one taken

explanation.surface: Henry VIII and his wives, leaving out his final Catherine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' strips HENRY to HY; 'excepting' removes the E that ends 'Catherine' from BRIDES. Henry VIII's last wife was Catherine Parr.
explanation.definitionFit: Hybrids are offspring of mixed parentage, so they come of varied stock.

clue.text: Soldier, an officer not entirely feeling the loss of his company

indicators.note: not entirely means the last letter is dropped

parts.words: feeling the loss of his company

explanation.surface: An officer separated from his unit feels the loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' trims LONELY to LONEL. 'his company' looks like a military unit but means companionship.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonel is a senior army officer, a soldier of high rank.

clue.text: Nigel wrongly obtained items from 6

indicators.note: wrongly signals the letters of the name are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Nigel acquired objects improperly from a site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges NIGEL. Lord Elgin removed the marbles from the Parthenon on the Athens citadel at 6, and 'wrongly' nods to the dispute over them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Earl of that title shipped the Parthenon marbles to Britain, taking them from Athens.

clue.text: Arrange date with Rambo, as being a desirable type

indicators.note: arrange signals putting the letters in a new order

explanation.surface: Fixing up a date with Rambo, considered quite a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrange' rearranges DATE RAMBO.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamboat is an attractive person, someone very desirable.
